posts.title: Insurance Company Settlement Calculators
posts.excerpt: Settlement calculators for State Farm, Progressive, GEICO, Allstate, USAA and other major auto insurers, with how each handles injury claims.
posts.content:
A rough estimate, not a prediction or an offer. ClaimValuator is not affiliated with any insurance company listed here. Real settlements depend on the facts, the insurance available and negotiation.

Calculators by insurance company

Market share is private passenger auto direct premiums written in 2025, from NAIC data published by the Insurance Information Institute. Nationwide, Mercury and Erie are outside the top ten.

Is it your insurer or theirs?

The same company can be on either side of your claim, and the rules change with it.

  • The other driver’s insurer handles a third-party claim against its policyholder’s liability coverage. Its adjuster works for the policyholder, and it usually pays no more than the policy limit.
  • Your own insurer handles first-party claims: PIP in no-fault states, MedPay, collision, and uninsured or underinsured motorist coverage. Your policy is a contract, so you have to cooperate, and in return the insurer owes you a duty of good faith.

How insurers value injury claims

No major insurer publishes its formula, but adjusters generally start with documented losses (medical bills, future care, lost pay), add an amount for pain and suffering based on the injury and its treatment, reduce the total for your share of the fault and cap it at the policy limit. Many large insurers use valuation software, Colossus being the best-known example, which scores what is in the medical records. Gaps in treatment and missing records tend to lower the result, so documentation matters more than anything you say to the adjuster.

What J.D. Power’s 2026 claims study found

J.D. Power’s 2026 U.S. Auto Claims Satisfaction Study surveyed 8,261 customers who settled a claim between September 2025 and August 2026. It measures how policyholders rate their own insurer’s claims service, not how much injury claims pay.

  • The industry average held at 700 out of 1,000. Amica scored highest (775), followed by Nationwide (743) and the Automobile Club of Southern California (740).
  • 26% of claims were total losses, up from 16% four years earlier. Satisfaction with total-loss claims has fallen 46 points since 2023.
  • A quarter of total-loss customers with a car loan were paid less than they owed. Those customers gave the lowest score in the study, 490.
  • Customers who said the insurer gave them a seamless experience across phone, app and web scored 804; those who disagreed scored 390. Insurers managed that only 54% of the time.
  • The average repair took 15.3 days in early 2026, ten days faster than in early 2024.

If your car was totaled, our total loss calculator helps you check the insurer’s valuation, and the diminished value calculator covers cars that were repaired.

How to check an insurer’s complaint record

  1. Open the NAIC Consumer Insurance Search and search for the company by name.
  2. Choose the company that wrote the policy. Large insurers have several companies, and the one on the policy declarations page is the one to check.
  3. Look at closed complaints by state and by type, such as claim delays or unsatisfactory settlement offers, for the past three years.
  4. To complain yourself, contact your state insurance department. Keep copies of your letters, emails and the adjuster’s notes.

Questions people ask

Which insurance company pays the most for injury claims?

No insurer publishes what it pays on injury claims, and payouts depend far more on the injury, the documentation, fault and policy limits than on the company. Be skeptical of sites that rank insurers by “average settlement”: there is no public data set that supports those numbers.

Can I file a claim with the other driver’s insurer if I am not its customer?

Yes. Every insurer takes claims against its policyholders. Several, including State Farm, Progressive, USAA, Liberty Mutual, Travelers and American Family, have online routes for non-customers; others ask you to call. Each calculator page above lists the route.

Do I need a lawyer to deal with the insurance company?

Not for every claim. Small claims with minor injuries often settle directly. A lawyer is worth talking to if the injury is serious, fault is disputed, the offer is close to the policy limit or the insurer stops responding. Our attorney fee calculator shows what you would keep after fees.

What is Colossus?

Colossus is claims-valuation software used by insurers to score injury claims from the medical records, bills and other data an adjuster enters. It is the best-known product of its kind. Because it works from the records, missing documents and gaps in treatment tend to lower the result.

Sources

  • Insurance Information Institute, Facts + Statistics: Insurance company rankings (private passenger auto, 2025 direct premiums written, NAIC data via S&P Global)
  • J.D. Power, 2026 U.S. Auto Claims Satisfaction Study (press release, Oct. 27, 2026)
  • NAIC Consumer Insurance Search (complaints by company, state and type)
  • NAIC, state insurance department contacts
  • NAIC, How to file a complaint and research complaints against insurance carriers

Checked October 2026.
